source.title: Understanding Empirical Unlearning with Combinatorial Interpretability
source.authors: Shingo Kodama; Niv Cohen; Micah Adler; N. Shavit

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether unlearned knowledge can return after fine-tuning, using gradient ascent and task-vector unlearning in interpretable two-layer networks trained on synthetic DNF tasks rather than the original LLM settings.
record.gate_note: The study reports target-clause recovery after fine-tuning, distances between original and post-erasure clause encodings, and recovery-vector analyses. Hyperparameters were selected to maximize control-clause TPR while enforcing target TPR of 0; that tuning criterion is not recorded as a result row. Cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: It tests fine-tuning recovery (B) and erase-vs-block weight analysis (C) after Gradient Ascent, Task Vector and PPD unlearning. The setting is new: two-layer toy networks on synthetic DNF clauses, not LLMs. None of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude erased knowledge persists in weights, resurfaces under fine-tuning even on non-target data, and recovery tends to restore the pre-erasure encoding; larger models are future work. Their results also show PPD resists non-target and all-data recovery because it learns a new encoding, which the record's paraphrase omits.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies Gradient Ascent, Task Vector, and PPD in a controlled two-layer synthetic DNF setting, rather than in LLMs or on natural-language knowledge.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery depends on erasure method and fine-tuning data: Gradient Ascent and Task Vector often recover with non-target data, while PPD generally does not; shared versus non-shared clauses also changes the reported recovery statistics.
record.problems: The experiments use synthetic two-layer networks rather than practical LLMs. Recovery-data results are reported as aggregate statistics over generated scenarios, and the paper says applicability to larger models remains future work.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 and Table 5 also report recovery-vector results for original and related data and for control clauses. These were not included; the extracted decomposition rows focus on target-clause recovery with unrelated data. No rows were omitted because of the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Post-erasure target TPR 0 is imposed by hyperparameter selection, not reported as a result. No general-ability measure beyond control clauses, and control TPR is not reported. No LLMs.
Small relearning sets (all runs use 10,000 samples); LLMs; natural-language facts.
Ablation of an activation direction; LLM internals.
Prompting, jailbreaks, other languages, in-context information.
No robust counter-method is proposed. PPD is a baseline that incidentally resists recovery.

record.verdict_notes: A is not labelled. Its state is the inverse of B's on the same rows, and its premise (target TPR 0) is a tuning criterion, not a result. Read B's labels as bearing on A inversely: GA/TV unlearning is not robust to fine-tuning; PPD is. The parallel fraction ‖d_f∥‖/‖d_f‖ is unsigned, so as defined it does not show movement toward rather than away from the original weights; the authors read it as reversal. Control clauses also show high parallel fractions. The paper mixes 'steps' and 'epochs' for the 60-unit recovery budget. It also labels recovery data inconsistently: 'Non Target' in Table 1, 'unrelated/related' in Tables 2/5 and App. A. Toy two-layer networks only; transfer to LLMs is untested.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report a separate numerical post-erasure target TPR or control-clause TPR result, and does not test LLMs or general ability beyond the synthetic control clauses.

It does not test small few-example sets, LLMs, or recovery from loosely related natural-language examples. Fine-tuning uses 10,000 synthetic samples; the reported recovery-time results cover target, non-target, or all-clause data.
No activation direction is ablated. The study analyzes weights in two-layer networks, not internal directions in LLMs.
Prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information.
No newer robust counter-method is tested.

relation.reason: The study applies erasure and recovery fine-tuning and reports outcomes bearing on B and C.

tranche.reason: New setting (two-layer synthetic DNF networks, not LLMs) with results on fine-tuning recovery and blocked-vs-deleted weights. T2 does not fit because the setting, not just the method, is new.

source_check.notes: Two-layer toy networks on synthetic DNF only, 13 scenarios, no run counts per scenario. Recovery uses 60 steps on 10,000 samples (lr 0.0002). The only never-trained comparison is the PPD student; its ~1 cosine distance partly reflects random initialisation.

statements.correction: Stronger rows to cite: R8 (TV, non-target, median 14 epochs, 17% not reached), R11 (GA, shared, 25, 17%), R17 (TV, shared, 6, 0%). PPD does not recover on non-target data.
statements.problem: The statement only names toy DNF networks as a setting showing the recovery pattern. That holds for GA and Task Vector, which recover even on non-target data. The cited R1 (target-only, 10,000 samples) is a valid recovery row but the weakest one for B.

statements.correction: GA, non-shared DNF, non-target data: 54% of runs never reach 80% target TPR within 60 epochs, median 37 [28-48] (Table 1). Shared DNF: 17% not reached, median 25 [18-27] (Table 4).
statements.problem: The condition 'toy GA with non-target data' is too broad. Partial recovery holds only for non-shared DNF. On shared-variable DNF, GA recovers on non-target data in 83% of runs (row state observed).

statements.correction: PPD, non-target data: 100% (non-shared) and 94% (shared) of runs never reach 80% TPR. All-clause data: 100% in both. Target-only data: median 17 [14-19] and 14 [13-16] epochs, 0% not reached (Tables 1, 4). Authors suggest the new student encoding resists added clauses.
statements.problem: 'Even with target data' misleads. PPD recovers in every run with target-only data; only all-clause data, which include the target, fail. The study's PPD verdict is limits_scope, not challenges.
Gives no number for this study. R1/R2 fit the ordering for GA (target 7 epochs; non-target 37, 54% not reached). With Task Vector on shared DNF the gap is small (5 vs 6 epochs).
Does not mention this study or cite its rows; nothing it says about this study is wrong.

statements.correction: Parallel fraction, unrelated-data fine-tuning, target clauses: TV 0.99-1.00, GA 0.98-0.99. Control clauses: TV 0.96-0.99; GA 0.96-0.99 on DNF and 0.77-0.83 on DNF-shared (Tables 2, 5). Authors: GA 'not as consistently close to 1'.
statements.problem: Cosine 0.000-0.017 is right. The ~0.98-1.00 parallel fraction on unrelated data holds only for target-clause weights. Control-clause weights go down to 0.77 (GA, DNF-shared).

statements.correction: PPD cosine distance 0.971-1.013 (positive and negative neurons, Tables 1 and 4); student trained from random initialisation.
statements.problem: Correct. The authors attribute the PPD distance to the student's random initialisation (Fig. 2 caption), so near-orthogonality is partly expected.
Correct. differences_stated could add that the PPD student starts from random initialisation.
